svg.title: K3 — Drum and belt line: mechanisms
svg.text: K3 — Drum and belt line: how the mechanisms work
Section views, simplified; each panel loops on its own. Numbers from the concept document [E].

g.text: 1 Drum tilts about its own pouring lip
The tilt axis runs through the lowest point of the mouth rim, so the
pouring point stays fixed for every angle. One point feeds the pot
on the deck, the extended belt nose (30 mm lower) and the cutter
2 Inside the drum: wash, peel, spin
The wall turns, the helix fin keeps the charge in. To peel, a loose
knurled disc lies on the floor and the tool arm holds a scraper
still in the charge, so potatoes roll over the disc instead of
riding round with the wall. Slurry goes to the gutter.
2–500 rpm, 30 Nm · 1.5 kg peeled in 3 min
3 Belt under fixed gates: cut and lay down
The belt carries the item under the gates. G2 holds it, G1's blade
passes 0.5 mm in front of the nose bar and never touches the belt;
slices fall into the vessel below. To lay a cutlet or sheet down
flat, the nose runs out over the pan and pulls back at belt speed.
4 Roll pocket: the belt rolls a Roulade
slice with filling on its first third
rollers close, belt runs: slice rolls up
pocket opens, roll leaves seam down
No gripper: the belt itself forms the pocket. The top strand sags
into a loop between two rollers, the filled slice runs in, the
rollers close and the running belt turns it on itself, contained all
round. The same pocket rolls mince and dough into logs for patties,
loop inner Ø 45–65 · 30 s per pair of rolls
deck H0: 3 kW hob on 3 load cells
head brings the hot cover pan, rim down
rim to rim; socket takes both tangs
set down, upper pan lifted off
browned side up, second side fries
A weighing, heated lift deck and a handle gripper run on two sealed
mast tubes (magnet coupled, no wall seal). The head only grips the
tang on every vessel: it carries pots to the hobs and the oven,
pours by rolling and flips by inverting a pan pair.
head 10 kg at 200 mm · 25 s per flip
The drum washes itself with the lance jets and pours every liquor to
the gutter, then its own coil heats it empty to 110 °C. The belt is
washed on its return strand: scraper, spray bars on both faces, a
steam bar at 90–95 °C for 8–10 s, air knife.
drum 6 L, 9 min · belt 9–11 L, 8–10 min
